task.definition: Smallest unit of work with measurable completion: produces testable code or configuration change, has a review gate, can be evaluated independently of prior tasks.
not_examples: Write failing test (this is a step, not a task)
Run test (this is a step within a task)

step.definition: Single action within a task, executable in 2-5 minutes of focused work, with visible input/output.
not_examples: Implement authentication (this is a task, contains multiple steps)

command.definition: Explicit instruction: either a shell invocation (bash, git) or a CLI flag. Commands are deterministic and executable.
not_examples: Conclusion first (this is a directive, not a command)

directive.definition: Guiding principle from CLAUDE.md or project rules. Directives shape decision-making, not deterministic execution.
not_examples: git commit (this is a command, not guidance)

hook.definition: Event-triggered script in ~/.claude/hooks/. Fires on Claude Code lifecycle event (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, etc.).
not_examples: superpowers plugin (plugins are extensions, hooks are local scripts)

skill.definition: Callable capability bundled in a plugin. Has a name (e.g., superpowers:writing-plans) and parameters. Invokes via Skill tool.
not_examples: Agent (agents are different: fresh context, open-ended reasoning)

agent.definition: Subagent spawned via Agent tool: fresh context, specialized for a task type (code-reviewer, explore, etc.). Different from skill.
not_examples: Skill (skills run in session context, agents have fresh context)

plugin.definition: Installed extension from a marketplace (e.g., superpowers, context7). Loaded at session start, provides skills or MCP servers.
not_examples: Hook (hooks are user scripts; plugins are packaged extensions)

worktree.definition: Isolated git working copy of the repo, created via superpowers:using-git-worktrees. Used for parallel feature branches. Located at .worktrees/
not_examples: Branch (branch is git concept; worktree is git + filesystem isolation)

session.definition: One conversation with Claude Code. Starts at session ID, ends at Stop hook trigger. Has one model, one context window.
not_examples: Task (session may contain many tasks; task is code work unit)

model.definition: Claude variant handling inference: haiku (fast, cheap), sonnet (balanced), opus (capable, slow). Set in settings.json::model.
not_examples: Agent (model is the LLM; agent is a dispatch pattern)

token_cost.definition: Approximate inference price per command invocation, estimated from context size and model. Used to measure harness efficiency.
not_examples: Wall-clock time (different metric; can be decoupled)
